correctness.rationale: For any q,k>=2, cyclic spacing q gives alpha=k and a unique longer gap q+1 for each maximum independent set, so exactly n=kq+1 sets I_j. The gcd(q,n)=1 permutes them to all consecutive length-k circular arcs; a transversal has each circular selected gap <=k. A marked-vertex count gives n/t times bounded positive compositions, and deficits for t=q+1 give n/(q+1)*binom(k+q-1,q). An independent original-graph brute-force verifier confirms all cardinality coefficients in 14 small instances, and an independent DP confirms larger composition counts. No finite test is used to infer a universal assertion.

value.rationale: The one-defect family n=kq+1 has a canonical first surplus gap. The result exhibits a structural isomorphism of its entire maximum-independent-set hypergraph to the length-k cyclic interval hypergraph and determines every labelled transversal coefficient, the sharp deletion threshold h=q+1, and the exact count n/(q+1)*binom(k+q-1,q) of optimizers for an infinite two-parameter graph family. This answers a natural refinement of the recent hitting-set problem; it is not a numerical table or a mere restatement of a general bound.
